records.name: Philadelphia Mineralogical Society
records.summary: Rock, mineral and fossil fans who meet each month for a guest speaker, take collecting trips and visit private collections, and hold a yearly show.
records.what_you_do: Attend the monthly talks, join collecting and collection-visit trips, and take part in the spring mineral show.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the second Thursday, doors open at 7 pm and the talk starts at 7:30 pm, in person or on Zoom

cost.text: Membership cost is not listed on the site

first_step.how: Come to a public monthly meeting, or use the Join Now link on the society site
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to the public and membership is open to anyone interested in earth sciences, but the site does not describe a beginner program

records.notes: The old phillyrocks.org address redirects to the society site. The page lists a September 10 meeting without a year. The meeting room is not named on the page, so check the site before going.

records.name: Delaware Valley Paleontological Society
records.summary: Fossil fans, from beginners to working scientists, who meet most months at the Academy of Natural Sciences, go on fossil digging trips, and run a yearly Fossil Fair.
records.what_you_do: Go to the monthly talks, join field trips to fossil sites, and take part in the yearly Fossil Fair.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the fourth Thursday, September to June, at the Academy of Natural Sciences; the start time is not on the site

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the site

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page on the society site to ask how to join or visit
first_step.basis: Membership comes with a newsletter, but the site does not say whether meetings are open to visitors or how a newcomer starts

records.notes: The site has no dated items, so the status is a judgment from a working site. The start time, dues and a contact email are not on the page. Not confirmed by a second source.

records.name: Rittenhouse Astronomical Society
records.summary: An astronomy society founded in 1888 that runs public talks with guest speakers and keeps the public posted through a mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Attend the public talks and guest speakers, and get event news from the mailing list.

schedule.text: Monthly public events and talks; the site does not give days or times

cost.text: Cost is not stated on the site

first_step.how: Join the mailing list through the club's contact page
first_step.basis: The club says no experience is needed to attend and gives a simple way to sign up for updates

records.notes: The newest dated item on the about page is from 1988 and the other event listings are undated or older, so there is no recent dated proof. Status rests on a working site. The meeting place and days are not on the site. Recent events were held on Zoom according to the JPL club page.

leads_only.note: Meetup group for weekend conversation sessions on philosophy, science and other topics. Meetup is lead only; not read beyond the search listing.

leads_only.name: Science on Tap Philadelphia

leads_only.note: Only a 2015 grant listing was found. No sign of current activity.

leads_only.note: Named on a list as running lectures and an annual field trip. The domain did not resolve when fetched, so it was not checked further.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Shell Club
leads_only.note: Named on the museum outside clubs list and a search snippet as having monthly speakers and a spring auction. No own site found; the museum page returned a 301.

leads_only.note: Non-credit learning program for adults 50 and older. Location and whether it serves Philadelphia residents are not confirmed.

notes: Lane G science and learning sweep, 10 of 10 WebSearch calls used, about 19 WebFetch calls. Three records written, all publish. Most science offers in Philadelphia are museum or university programs (Academy of Natural Sciences, Franklin Institute observatory nights, Drexel Lynch Observatory first-Wednesday public nights from a 2019 era article) rather than community groups, so they were left out, except where a group runs its own program. The Free Library Thought Club is the strongest philosophy lead but its pages are blocked. Philadelphia Mineralogical Society and Delaware Valley Paleontological Society were the best fossil and geology finds. Delaware Astronomical Society (Greenville, DE) and West Jersey Astronomical Society (NJ) were not recorded because they are not Philadelphia based. Astronomy Enthusiasts of Lancaster County is outside the city and was not recorded. Stronger coverage of adult learning and talks would need more searches.
